text:
alex: Heads-up: saw a customer report where they got charged twice after a reconnect + prefetch + truncate sequence. attaching quick trace.

maria: Ugh. Do we have a repro? Which route / model? :thinking_face:

alex: Small repro on canary. Route: /v1/generate -> we prefetch embeddings in background, then stream. Steps: client reconnects mid-stream, server does suffix truncate, then prefetch heartbeat writes a provisional ledger entry during resume.

chen: Can you paste the tracelet? a couple lines is fine.

alex: Sure. snippet:
```
[2024-06-03T12:05:22Z] stream:start session=abc123
[2024-06-03T12:05:24Z] prefetch:heartbeat provisional_token=tok-pre-xyz
[2024-06-03T12:05:25Z] client:reconnect session=abc123 resume=true
[2024-06-03T12:05:26Z] stream:truncate suffix_len=42
[2024-06-03T12:05:26Z] ledger:commit provisional_token=tok-pre-xyz -> confirmed
```

maria: From that snippet it looks like the provisional entry from prefetch is getting confirmed after truncation but our confirmation path doesn't check for suffix ownership overlap = fencepost.

jon: Right — we have two different subsystems (prefetcher and stream reconciler) racing to claim the same token window. One marks provisional, the other confirms post-truncate. If confirmation happens after we trim suffix, we end up crediting both the trimmed suffix and the resumed tokens.

sre-bot: alert: high-sev billing drift detected on canary, tag: double-credit

chen: We should probably: 1) make confirmation idempotent by verifying snapshot-consumer-offset matches expected; 2) or attach a session-change tombstone to provisional entries on truncate so confirm rejects.

maria: Both sound reasonable. Which is lower friction? Adding extra check on confirm is small but could still allow a race if snapshot state lags.

alex: I'd prefer tombstone on truncate — it's explicit and prevents late confirms. Steps: on stream:truncate write tombstone key provisional_token -> tombstoned. confirm path checks tombstone flag before committing.

jon: Concern: tombstones increase write amplification and complicate GC. We'll need a background compactor to evict old tombstones after session TTL.

chen: Another angle: change prefetch to use ephemeral provisional IDs scoped to session nonce so a resume creates a new nonce and old provisionals are auto-ignored by confirm. That avoids tombstones but requires handshake change.

maria: Handshake change touches clients; not ideal. Tombstone + compactor seems safe and internal.

alex: I'll prototype tombstone approach and add metric: confirm_rejected_tombstone_count. If we see many rejections, we can consider changing prefetch id allocation.

jon: Also add console dashboard panel: "provisional lifecycle" showing provisional->confirm->tombstone rates and average latency between provisional and confirm. Helps ops tune.

maria: Good. For canary: add a temporary rule to hold confirms for 250ms to surface race more deterministically in logs (non-prod only).

chen: Testcases: replay the trace with truncated confirm arriving late; assert no double-charge (ledger delta == single). Also add fuzz where prefetch heartbeat lands before/after reconnect.

alex: I'll open a PR with code + unit tests + migration for tombstone compactor. pinging @jon for review once PR is up.

jon: ack. Also add a note in console rollouts doc: "billing reconciler will treat tombstoned provisionals as invalid confirms" so CS doesn't get surprised by provisional rejections.

maria: Thanks team. Let's watch canary for the next 24h after deploy.

alex: will do. :thumbsup:
